title: Direct session display route drops the supported `none` status view
reasoning: The non-id display route treats `status_view === 'none'` as a valid display preference and suppresses overlays/messages while still rendering parts and explanations. The id-scoped display route resolves the same `statusView` preference shape, but its search validator only accepts `full`, `pages_only`, and `posture_only`. As a result, a direct URL such as `/sessions/123/display?status_view=none` is silently normalized to the default `full`, so overlays/messages remain enabled. Token configs can still carry `none`, making direct search parameters inconsistent with the same display behavior elsewhere.
recommendation: Add `none` to the accepted `status_view` values in `app/routes/sessions.$id.display.tsx` and mirror the `isNoneView` handling from `sessions.display.tsx` so direct and token-backed display preferences behave consistently.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests for `sessions.$id.display` only verify the default render and loading state. The broader `sessions.display` tests cover token preferences for `pages_only` and `posture_only`, but no test exercises `status_view=none` as a direct search parameter on the id-scoped route.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route test for `/sessions/456/display?status_view=none` that mocks an active session and asserts `StatusOverlay` and notification `Message` are not rendered while the session parts and explanation indicator still render.
minimumFixScope: Update `app/routes/sessions.$id.display.tsx` search validation and render gating for `status_view: 'none'`; add one focused route test.
